brainstorm:
Decided: no provision-level mapping to RMiT. General cross-reference only, because RMiT numbering shifts on reissue and a pinned reference would go stale.
Decided: phase milestones stay unprescribed in the PD. PayNet owns the detailed implementation plan with the pilot banks, and BNM PDs stay principle-based where possible.
Decided: consent expiry is uniform across all data subjects. No separate regime for business customers — the PDPA draws no such distinction and a split would fragment the dashboard.
Decided: participation stays banking-only for phase two. Non-bank extension is a sequencing decision, not an omission.
Decided: the real-time consent dashboard is a standing requirement, not a phase-two enhancement.

For each: find the evidence that supports it, or the peer practice that contradicts it. Do not reopen the decision itself.
draft:
Follow the standard PD skeleton: 1 Introduction, 2 Applicability, 3 Legal provisions, 4 Effective date, 5 Interpretation, then the substantive parts.
Number standards as S 1.1 and guidance as G 1.2. Keep the S and G prefixes visible in every paragraph reference.
Put definitions in Interpretation only, never inline in a substantive paragraph.
write:
Obligations read "must". Guidance reads "should". Never mix the two in one paragraph.
Do not introduce a defined term outside the Interpretation part.
Keep paragraphs to one obligation each. Prefer the active voice and name the obligated party.
Stay principle-based: state the outcome required, not the implementation.
deliver: First sign-off by Deputy Director, second sign-off by Director.
